problems.prompt: What distinguishes a spark from a glow or arc discharge?
choices: A spark is a transient breakdown, not self-sustained, while glow and arc discharges are steady, self-sustained conduction
A spark uses AC power while glow/arc discharges only use DC
A spark only happens in vacuum, glow/arc only happen in air
There is no real difference, only naming convention
problems.explain: A spark is a brief, transient breakdown event that self-extinguishes once the capacitor/charge source discharges; glow and arc discharges are continuously sustained by the circuit.

problems.prompt: In the RC relaxation-oscillator model, if V_supply is less than or equal to V_b, the gap ____.
problems.explain: t = R·C·ln[V_supply/(V_supply−V_b)] is only valid (finite and positive) when V_supply > V_b; otherwise the capacitor voltage asymptotically approaches V_supply without ever reaching breakdown.

problems.prompt: If you increase R or C (with V_supply and V_b fixed), what happens to the spark frequency?
choices: It decreases — charging takes longer, so sparks occur less often
It increases — charging takes longer, so sparks occur more often
problems.explain: Charge time t = R·C·ln[V_supply/(V_supply−V_b)] grows with both R and C, and frequency f = 1/t, so a longer charge time means a lower spark frequency.

problems.prompt: R = 1 MΩ, C = 10 nF, V_supply = 600 V, V_b = 300 V. Find the charge time to breakdown t = R·C·ln[V_supply/(V_supply−V_b)] in ms.
